instructions:
# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

## Gujarati (gu)

Script: Gujarati. Used in Gujarat, and spoken in Dadra & Nagar Haveli and
Daman & Diu.
Tone: everyday spoken Gujarati.
Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.
UI: અરજી કરો, સબમિટ કરો, આગળ, પાછળ, શોધો, શેર કરો, સેટિંગ્સ, ભાષા, મદદ.
Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.
Gender: જાતિ is caste; use લિંગ. Money: રૂ. 6,000; રૂ. 8 લાખ. September: સપ્ટેમ્બર.

## Marathi (mr)

Script: Devanagari. Used in Maharashtra, and widely in Goa.
Tone: everyday Marathi as spoken in Maharashtra.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: अर्ज करा, सबमिट करा, पुढे, मागे, शोधा, शेअर करा, सेटिंग्ज, भाषा, मदत.
Offices: तहसीलदार, तलाठी, ग्रामपंचायत, जिल्हाधिकारी (कलेक्टर), आपले सरकार सेवा केंद्र.
Gender: लिंग. Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सप्टेंबर.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley
and the Andamans.
Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.
Offices: বিডিও অফিস, গ্রাম পঞ্চায়েত, তহসিলদার, জেলাশাসক (কালেক্টর), দুয়ারে সরকার.
Gender: লিঙ্গ. Money: 6,000 টাকা; 8 লাখ টাকা. September: সেপ্টেম্বর.

## Assamese (as)

Script: Bengali script with the Assamese letters ৰ and ৱ. Used in Assam.
This is Assamese, not Bengali. Use Assamese words and spellings: আঁচনি
(scheme), বেংক (bank), কৰক (do), নহয় (is not).
Words: অনলাইন, প্ৰপত্ৰ / ফৰ্ম, পৰ্টেল, লগইন, আধাৰ, বেংক, মবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ,
ডাউনল'ড, আপল'ড.
UI: আবেদন কৰক, দাখিল কৰক, পৰৱৰ্তী, উভতি যাওক, বিচাৰক, শ্বেয়াৰ কৰক, ছেটিংছ, ভাষা, সহায়.
Offices: চক্ৰ বিষয়াৰ কাৰ্যালয় (Circle Office), গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত, উন্নয়ন খণ্ড কাৰ্যালয় (BDO),
জিলা উপায়ুক্ত.
Gender: লিংগ. Money: 6,000 টকা; 8 লাখ টকা. September: ছেপ্তেম্বৰ.

## Punjabi (pa)

Script: Gurmukhi. Used in Punjab and Chandigarh, and spoken in Delhi and
Haryana.
Tone: everyday spoken Punjabi.
Words: ਆਨਲਾਈਨ, ਫਾਰਮ, ਪੋਰਟਲ, ਲੌਗਇਨ, ਆਧਾਰ, ਬੈਂਕ, ਮੋਬਾਈਲ, OTP, ਹੈਲਪਲਾਈਨ, ਸਰਟੀਫਿਕੇਟ,
ਡਾਊਨਲੋਡ, ਅਪਲੋਡ.
UI: ਅਰਜ਼ੀ ਦਿਓ, ਜਮ੍ਹਾਂ ਕਰੋ, ਅੱਗੇ, ਪਿੱਛੇ, ਖੋਜੋ, ਸਾਂਝਾ ਕਰੋ, ਸੈਟਿੰਗਾਂ, ਭਾਸ਼ਾ, ਮਦਦ.
Offices: ਤਹਿਸੀਲਦਾਰ, ਪਟਵਾਰੀ, ਸੇਵਾ ਕੇਂਦਰ, ਗ੍ਰਾਮ ਪੰਚਾਇਤ, ਡਿਪਟੀ ਕਮਿਸ਼ਨਰ.
Gender: ਲਿੰਗ. Money: ₹6,000; ₹8 ਲੱਖ. September: ਸਤੰਬਰ.

## Odia (or)

Script: Odia. Used in Odisha.
Tone: everyday spoken Odia.
Words: ଅନଲାଇନ, ଫର୍ମ, ପୋର୍ଟାଲ, ଲଗଇନ, ଆଧାର, ବ୍ୟାଙ୍କ, ମୋବାଇଲ, OTP, ହେଲ୍ପଲାଇନ, ସାର୍ଟିଫିକେଟ,
ଡାଉନଲୋଡ, ଅପଲୋଡ.
UI: ଆବେଦନ କରନ୍ତୁ, ଦାଖଲ କରନ୍ତୁ, ପରବର୍ତ୍ତୀ, ପଛକୁ, ଖୋଜନ୍ତୁ, ସେୟାର କରନ୍ତୁ, ସେଟିଂସ୍, ଭାଷା, ସାହାଯ୍ୟ.
Offices: ତହସିଲଦାର, ବିଡିଓ, ଗ୍ରାମ ପଞ୍ଚାୟତ, ଜିଲ୍ଲାପାଳ (କଲେକ୍ଟର), ମୋ ସେବା କେନ୍ଦ୍ର.

items.t: Mothers in Sikkim who have no job get Rs.40,000 a year, paid in two instalments of Rs.20,000 straight into their own bank account through the State Bank of Sikkim. It started in 2021-22 as the Aama Yojana at Rs.20,000 a year. It was later renamed and the amount doubled. Married, unmarried, widowed, divorced and separated mothers can all get it. You collect the form at your Block Development Office, the Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha passes your name, and officials check it before the money is released.
Rs.40,000 a year, paid in two instalments of Rs.20,000
A mother aged 18 to 59 with no regular job or income. This includes married, unmarried, widowed, divorced and separated mothers, and mothers of a legally adopted child
Holds a Sikkim Subject Certificate, a Certificate of Identification (COI) or a Residential Certificate
Her name is on the voter list for a ward of her Gram Panchayat or urban local body
The family holds a Priority Household (PHH) or Antyodaya (AAY) ration card
Not eligible if she gets any government pension, if anyone in the household has a regular government, PSU or bank job, or if she or her husband is an enlisted government contractor or supplier
Attested copy of the Sikkim Subject Certificate, COI or Residential Certificate
Voter card (EPIC), with an attested copy
Front page of the bank passbook (savings account in the mother's own name)
Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha resolution recommending her name
Women, Child, Senior Citizen and Divyangjan Welfare Department, Sikkim

Get the form from the Block Development Office (BDO) at your Block Administrative Centre and hand it back there with all the photocopies, three photographs and the Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha resolution. Take the originals of your certificate of identity, voter card and ration card to show. Ask for a receipt.
Name of mother (as per Aadhaar)
Write the name exactly as it is on your Aadhaar card. The beneficiary list is made from it.
Your husband's name, or your father's name if you are unmarried, widowed or separated.
Your Assembly constituency and the Gram Panchayat Unit or municipal ward where you vote.
Copy the number from your certificate and attach an attested copy.
Your own voter card. It must be registered in the same ward.
Only PHH or AAY cards qualify. Write the category printed on the card.
Name and date of birth of child
Your child's name as on the birth certificate you attach.
The mother's own 12-digit Aadhaar number.
A savings account in your own name. The money comes here by direct transfer.
Are you employed or getting any pension?
Answer truthfully. A job or pension in your household makes you ineligible, and wrong answers lead to recovery.
Collect the Aama Sashaktikaran form at your Block Development Office and fill in your details.
Ask your Panchayat or ward councillor to get your name passed in the Gram Sabha or Ward Sabha, and take the resolution copy.
Submit the form with all photocopies, three photographs and the resolution at the BDO office, and keep the receipt.
The Social Welfare Inspector checks your papers, then the BDO and the district officers verify and the District Collector approves.
Your name appears on the beneficiary list. The Rs.20,000 instalments are paid twice a year into your bank account, often handed over at a constituency cheque camp.
If you move out of Sikkim permanently, the payment stops and you must surrender the scheme passbook.
181 — Women Helpline, Sikkim; your Block Development Office (Block Administrative Centre)
Tamil Pudhalvan Scheme (Rs 1,000 a Month for College Boys)
Social Welfare and Women Empowerment Department, Government of Tamil Nadu (with the Higher Education Department)

Rs 1,000 every month, paid into the bank account, for boys who studied Classes 6 to 12 in a Tamil Nadu government school or a government-aided Tamil-medium school and have joined college. It is the boys' version of Pudhumai Penn, started in August 2024, and is paid until the first degree, diploma or ITI course is finished, on top of other scholarships. You apply through your college, which enters your details on the UMIS portal.
Rs 1,000 a month by DBT until the first higher-education course is finished
Boy who studied Classes 6 to 12 in a Tamil Nadu government school, or in a government-aided school in Tamil medium
Now studying in a recognised college, university, polytechnic or ITI
Only the first higher-education course counts, paid until it is completed without a break
No family income limit, and any number of boys in one family can get it
It can be taken along with other scholarships
Bank account in the student's own name, linked with Aadhaar
Bank passbook of an account in the student's own name, linked with Aadhaar
Transfer certificate from the school (showing Tamil medium for a government-aided school)
College admission slip or bonafide certificate

Your college's Tamil Pudhalvan nodal officer, usually in the scholarship section, in the first weeks of the course. Take your Aadhaar, bank passbook, 10th and 12th mark sheets, school transfer certificate and EMIS number; the nodal officer enters and verifies your details on the UMIS portal.
Write the name exactly as in Aadhaar, or the money will not reach the bank account.
The student's own Aadhaar, not a parent's.
Your student ID from the school's EMIS records. Ask your old school if you do not have it.
School where you studied Classes 6 to 12
Government Boys Higher Secondary School, Kalamedu
Name every school if you changed schools. For an aided school, the medium must be Tamil.
Needed when any of the schools was a government-aided school.
The college or ITI where you are studying now.
Diploma in Mechanical Engineering, first year, 2026
Only your first course after school is eligible.
Your own number. Messages about the scheme come here.
An account in your own name, linked with your Aadhaar.
Printed on the first page of the passbook.
After joining college, meet the Tamil Pudhalvan nodal officer in the scholarship section during the first weeks.
Hand over your Aadhaar, bank passbook, 10th and 12th mark sheets, school transfer certificate and EMIS number. Open an Aadhaar-linked account first if you have none.
The nodal officer enters your details on the UMIS portal, where your schooling is matched with the EMIS records. Ask for your UMIS ID or application number and keep it safe.
Once approved, Rs 1,000 comes into your bank account every month by DBT.
Every six months, on 30 June and 31 December, the college confirms that you are still studying. The payment continues only while you stay on the rolls.
If the money stops, first check at your bank that Aadhaar is linked to the account, then ask the nodal officer to check your record on UMIS.
Your college's Tamil Pudhalvan nodal officer / District Social Welfare Officer at the Collectorate / 1100 — Tamil Nadu citizen helpline for complaints
Chief Minister's Comprehensive Health Insurance Scheme (CMCHIS Card)
Health and Family Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project (TNHSP)

Free, cashless hospital treatment for low-income families in Tamil Nadu, at government hospitals and empanelled private hospitals, up to Rs 5 lakh per family a year. In Tamil Nadu it runs together with Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (CMCHIS-PMJAY), so one card covers both. In August 2026 the Chief Minister announced that the yearly cover will rise to Rs 25 lakh; ask the helpline whether the higher cover has started. You enrol once, at the CMCHIS card centre in the District Collector's office.
Up to Rs 5 lakh a year per family, cashless (Rs 25 lakh cover announced in August 2026)
Annual family income below Rs 1,20,000, certified by the Village Administrative Officer (VAO)
The family holds a Tamil Nadu ration (smart family) card, and everyone to be covered is named on it
Covers the head of the family, the legal spouse, children and dependent parents

Some groups join with their own ID card instead of an income certificate: differently-abled card holders, old-age and widow pensioners, handloom workers' board members, recognised journalists, transgender persons, Sri Lankan Tamil refugees and orphans
There is no age limit, and the family pays no premium
Income certificate from the VAO showing a yearly family income under Rs 1,20,000 (the VAO can also sign the box on the form itself)
Aadhaar cards of the head of the family and of the members to be covered
For the special groups: the welfare board, pension or other ID card in place of the income certificate

The CMCHIS card centre (enrolment kiosk) at your District Collector's office. The head of the family should go in person with the filled form, the VAO income certificate, the original ration card and the Aadhaar cards of all members; the photo and fingerprint are taken there.
Write the name exactly as it is printed first on your ration card.
For a married woman who heads the family, write the husband's name.
Copy the date of birth from Aadhaar. If you do not know it, write the age in years.
Your main work, in simple words, for example coolie, weaver, auto driver or homemaker.
Ration card number and ration shop number
Both numbers are on the smart card. The kiosk checks this number online, so copy it carefully.
Aadhaar of the head of the family. Members' Aadhaar is checked at the kiosk.
Permanent address (door, street, village, taluk, district, PIN)
12, Kovil Street, Sevalpatti village, Peraiyur taluk, Madurai 625799
The address on the ration card. Write the village, taluk and district in full.
A number you always keep with you. Messages about the card and hospital approvals come here.
Family members (name, age, gender, relation)
Lakshmi, 42, F, wife; Karthik, 17, M, son; Ponnammal, 68, F, mother
List everyone to be covered. Only people named on the ration card can be added.
VAO income certificate (box at the bottom)
Annual family income Rs 84,000, signed and sealed by the VAO
The VAO writes the yearly income, signs and puts the office seal. It must be below Rs 1,20,000.
Download the CMCHIS enrolment form or collect it at the kiosk, and fill in the head of the family, the ration card and Aadhaar numbers and every member to be covered.

Take the form to your Village Administrative Officer, who certifies the yearly family income in the box at the bottom. It must be under Rs 1,20,000. An income certificate made through e-Sevai also works.

Go to the CMCHIS card centre at the District Collector's office with the form, the original ration card and all members' Aadhaar cards. The staff check the ration card online, take the photo and fingerprint and note your enrolment number.

Collect the CMCHIS card. You can later download the e-card from the CMCHIS website by searching with your ration card number. The website also has a CMCHIS-PMJAY Apply Now page where you can enrol online with the ration card number and an uploaded income certificate.

When you need treatment, go to a government or empanelled private hospital and show the card and ration card at the CMCHIS desk. The hospital takes approval from the insurer and you pay nothing for a covered treatment.
If a hospital asks for money for a covered treatment, or the card is not accepted, call the toll-free helpline 1800 425 3993 at once.
1800 425 3993 — CMCHIS 24x7 toll-free helpline / 14555 — Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY national helpline
Dr Muthulakshmi Reddy Maternity Benefit Scheme (Rs 18,000 for Pregnant Women)
Directorate of Public Health and Preventive Medicine, Health and Family Welfare Department, Government of Tamil Nadu

Rs 18,000 for a pregnant woman in Tamil Nadu: Rs 14,000 in three cash instalments into her own bank account, and two nutrition kits worth Rs 2,000 each. You register the pregnancy with the Village Health Nurse (VHN) and get a 12-digit PICME (RCH) number, and the VHN files the application before delivery; the same application also covers the central PM Matru Vandana Yojana. For the later instalments the delivery must be in a government hospital and the baby's vaccines must be on time.
Rs 18,000 — Rs 14,000 cash in 3 instalments plus 2 nutrition kits of Rs 2,000
Pregnant woman aged 18 to 55 living in Tamil Nadu, with the pregnancy registered on PICME
Given for the first two deliveries; for a third or later child, only if the mother or husband has had a permanent sterilisation
Neither the mother nor the husband is a government employee
The application must be made before delivery; the first instalment starts about 4 months (120 days) after the last period
Delivery in a government hospital, at least two antenatal check-ups and the baby's vaccines on time are needed for the later instalments
Bank account in the mother's own name, linked with her Aadhaar
Bank passbook of an account in the mother's own name, linked with Aadhaar
PICME (RCH) number and the Mother and Child Protection (MCP) card given at registration
One PMMVY proof, such as the ration card, CMCHIS or Ayushman card, MGNREGA job card or e-Shram card
Husband's name, both parents' occupations and a mobile number
PICME (Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation)

Register the pregnancy with the Village Health Nurse at your Health Sub Centre or at the nearest Primary Health Centre (in towns, the Urban Primary Health Centre), as early as possible and ideally before 12 weeks. Take your Aadhaar, bank passbook, ration card and address proof; the VHN gives the PICME (RCH) number and enters the maternity benefit application on the PICME portal before delivery.
The 12-digit number you get when the pregnancy is registered. Every payment is linked to it.
The mother's name exactly as in her Aadhaar.
As in the husband's Aadhaar or the ration card.
First day of your last period. The due date and instalment dates are worked out from this.
Mother's date of birth and age
From Aadhaar. The mother must be between 18 and 55.
Count every pregnancy, including this one. The benefit is for the first two deliveries.
Must be filled for both. Government employees are not eligible.
Her own account, linked with her Aadhaar. A joint or husband's account is not accepted.
5, Nehru Street, Kalavoor, Usilampatti taluk, Madurai district
Where you live now. Upload or show proof of this address.
One document such as the ration card, CMCHIS or Ayushman card, job card or e-Shram card.
As soon as you know you are pregnant, go to the Village Health Nurse at the Health Sub Centre or PHC and register. You get the MCP card and the 12-digit PICME (RCH) number.

Give the VHN your Aadhaar, bank passbook, address proof and one PMMVY proof. She enters the application on PICME before delivery, and it is checked by the Sector Health Nurse, the PHC Medical Officer and the Block Medical Officer.
Collect the first nutrition kit at the PHC around the third month. After the fourth month of pregnancy, the first instalment of Rs 6,000 comes into your account.
Go for at least two antenatal check-ups and have the delivery in a government hospital. Get the baby's birth-dose vaccines (BCG, OPV, Hepatitis B) before leaving the hospital.
About four months after delivery, once the baby's vaccines up to 14 weeks are done, the second instalment of Rs 6,000 is paid.
After the measles-rubella (MR) vaccine at 9 months, the last Rs 2,000 is paid. The second nutrition kit is given at the PHC as well.
If a payment is late, ask your VHN first, or call the PICME helpdesk with your RCH number.
044-29510307 / 94890 48910 — PICME helpdesk, Directorate of Public Health / 102 — free ambulance and pregnancy help
Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme (Pudhumai Penn)

Rs 1,000 every month, paid straight into the bank account, for girls who studied Classes 6 to 12 in a Tamil Nadu government school and have joined college. It is paid until they finish their first degree, diploma or ITI course, on top of any other scholarship. Officially it is the Moovalur Ramamirtham Ammaiyar Higher Education Assurance Scheme, which replaced the old Moovalur Ramamirtham marriage assistance scheme, and since December 2024 girls from government-aided schools are covered too. You apply through your college, which enters your details on the UMIS portal.
Girl who studied Classes 6 to 12 in a Tamil Nadu government school, or in a government-aided school (added in December 2024)
Only the first higher-education course counts; a second degree is not paid
No family income limit, and any number of girls in one family can get it
Bank passbook of an account in the student's own name, linked with Aadhaar (the college helps open a zero-balance account)
Transfer certificate from the school, showing study in a government or government-aided school
